falseFriends.actual: Use 'réel' or 'effectif', not 'actuel' (which means 'current/present-day'). In OEE context: 'valeur réelle' (actual value), not 'valeur actuelle' (current value).
falseFriends.performance: In OEE context, use 'rendement' per NF E60-182. 'Performance' in French can mean show/event. Note: 'taux de performance' is an accepted modern alternative used by AVEVA and some French vendors.
falseFriends.availability: Correct: 'disponibilité'. Common misspelling trap: 'availabilité' does not exist in French.
falseFriends.eventually: Use 'finalement' or 'en fin de compte', not 'éventuellement' (which means 'possibly/potentially')
falseFriends.assist: Use 'aider', not 'assister à' (which means 'to attend/witness'). 'Assister à une réunion' = to attend a meeting.
falseFriends.rate: In OEE/KPI context, use 'taux' (taux de disponibilité, taux de qualité). Not 'tarif' (price) or 'cadence' (throughput rate) unless context requires it.
falseFriends.setup: Use 'réglage' or 'préparation' for manufacturing setup. Not 'installation' (permanent machine install) or 'setup' (anglicism for software config).
falseFriends.idle: Use 'en attente' (waiting), 'en veille' (standby), or 'marche à vide' (running idle). Never 'paresseux' (lazy) for machine state.
falseFriends.billion: French 'billion' = 10^12 (long scale). For English billion (10^9), use 'milliard'. Critical for production statistics and financial KPIs.
falseFriends.station: 'Station' in French evokes train/petrol station. In manufacturing, 'poste de travail' (workstation) is clearer. Terms.json uses 'station' as a technical loanword — acceptable in MES context.
falseFriends.changeover: Use 'changement de série' or 'changement de production'. Bare 'changement' is too generic (could mean any change).

grammarNotes.genderAgreement: Technical terms: 'le TRS' (m), 'la disponibilité' (f), 'le rendement' (m), 'la qualité' (f), 'le temps de cycle' (m), 'l'équipe' (f), 'l'arrêt' (m), 'le rebut' (m). Article required in sentences: 'La disponibilité est de 85%'. Dropped in UI labels: 'Disponibilité: 85%'.
grammarNotes.articles: Use definite articles with metrics in running text: 'le TRS est de 85%'. Preposition 'de' before percentages: 'Le taux est de 85%' (not 'est 85%'). In UI labels and table headers, articles are omitted.
grammarNotes.prepositionalCompounds: French forms technical terms with 'de': 'temps de cycle', 'temps d'arrêt' (note elision: de+arrêt → d'arrêt), 'perte de vitesse', 'raison d'arrêt', 'changement de série'. Always check elision: 'de' + vowel → 'd''.
grammarNotes.numberFormatting: Decimal: comma (,). Thousands: thin space. Percentage: '85 %' (AFNOR with space) or '85%' (common in software UIs). Example: '1 234,56'. OEE display: 'Le TRS est de 85,3 %'.
grammarNotes.posteVsEquipe: 'Poste' = time-based shift slot ('travail en 3 postes' = 3-shift working). 'Équipe' = crew/team ('équipe de nuit' = night shift team). Terms.json uses 'Équipe' for shift (organizational unit) and 'temps de poste' for shift time (duration).
grammarNotes.compoundPluralModifiers: In prepositional compound phrases, the modifier noun after 'de' stays SINGULAR when naming a concept/category. CORRECT: 'causes de perte de cadence' (causes of loss [sg] of speed). WRONG: 'causes des pertes de cadence' (causes of-the losses [pl] of speed). The contracted article 'des' (de+les) signals incorrect pluralization of the modifier. Same pattern: 'raisons d'arrêt' (reasons of stop [sg]), not 'raisons des arrêts'. Only the head noun (causes, raisons, groupes) takes plural.

industryContext.oeeTerminology: TRS (Taux de Rendement Synthétique) is mandated by NF E60-182. OEE may appear in international contexts. Also: TRG (Taux de Rendement Global = OOE), TRE (Taux de Rendement Économique = TEEP). Practitioner preference: local_dominant — TRS is primary in all French manufacturing software.
industryContext.dominantVendors: SAP France, Dassault Systèmes DELMIA (French-origin), Schneider Electric AVEVA EcoStruxure (French-origin), Siemens Opcenter, Sage (SME)
industryContext.industrie40: France uses 'Industrie du futur' (Alliance Industrie du Futur, 2015) alongside 'Industrie 4.0'. Vocabulary: 'usine du futur', 'fabrication avancée', 'IoT industriel'.

commonMistakes: Using 'OEE' instead of 'TRS' in French UI — NF E60-182 mandates TRS. Also: OOE → TRO, TEEP → TRST.
Using 'performance' for OEE component without context — 'rendement' is the NF E60-182 term; 'taux de performance' is an accepted modern alternative.
Using 'actuel' for 'actual/measured' values — use 'réel' or 'effectif'. 'Actuel' means 'current/present'.
Writing 'availabilité' instead of 'disponibilité' — 'availabilité' does not exist in French.
Forgetting elision: 'temps de arrêt' → correct: 'temps d'arrêt'. 'de' + vowel = 'd'' in French.
Using informal 'tu' instead of formal 'vous' in all UI instructions and dialogs.
Decimal separator errors: '85.3%' should be '85,3 %' in French-locale display.

Pluralizing the modifier in compound noun phrases: 'causes des pertes de cadence' (WRONG — 'des pertes' pluralizes the modifier) instead of 'causes de perte de cadence' (CORRECT — 'perte' stays singular as it names the concept). The preposition 'de' + singular noun indicates category; 'des' (de+les) incorrectly pluralizes it
notes: Use TRS (Taux de Rendement Synthétique) per NF E60-182 standard — France is the only Romance-group language with a mandated national OEE acronym. Practitioner preference: local_dominant (TRS primary in all French manufacturing software). Formal 'vous' in all professional software. Note: 'rendement' (traditional, NF E60-182) and 'performance' (modern MES software) both used for OEE second component — flag for G3 native speaker confirmation.
